checks: Read original ce2469e6ba848252 §1, (1)–(3). The premise supplies a consistent stress and contact law. The claim does not infer existence of a pure abnormal stress at a general attained endpoint.

In the original cap coordinates the budget covector has offset −S_i and base Z_i. The coverage constraint enters with the opposite sign, giving the two moment equations. The residual on the sphere tangent annihilator is parallel to u_i, and both cap-plane support and contact complementarity make its component along u_i zero.

Common rotation changes the continuous variable by an orthogonal bijection and leaves the whole-space coverage value fixed. Its stationarity makes T symmetric by orthogonality to skew matrices. The contact balance gives P_V T=0, and T=T P_V since each u_i lies in V, so T=0.

With u_k in V, the projected moment equality suffices to integrate every affine L_k. The weighted contact laws have mass r_i S_i; all their points lie in the closed complements, and convexity puts the projected barycenter there. Their averaged base need not be integral.

overlap.comparison: Uses the same attained-span rotation and sphere calculus for an objective-one stress at a regular polytopal budget. The resulting tensor includes hinge and cap-volume terms. Its statement does not give the pure section system under a separately supplied zero-objective stress.

The actual-fiber-cover Fritz–John system allows a zero objective coefficient but its contact normal may be a nonzero fiber-normal-cone vector. This whole-space problem uses balanced saddle normals and common rotations to obtain a full summed zero tensor.

readability: The role of V is clear from the unit sphere and P_V notation. Calling V a linear subspace at its first occurrence would make this immediate.
